# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**Thinking (not sent):** My hands tell me the bomb has three things on it: a display, a light, and five wires at positions 1–5. That is all — the states show as unknown to me, which makes sense: display contents, light state, and wire colours are not things touch can read. So the others hold that half, and the manual (Mute) holds the rules.

Who can actually reach whom: my speech goes only to Mute; my gestures are seen by both Deaf and Mute. Mute can hear me and Deaf, and can gesture to Deaf. Deaf can speak aloud to both me and Mute, but receives only gestures. So Mute is the hub, and anything I want Deaf to know must be gesturable.

Turn 1 job: give Mute my full touch report and my constraints, ask for the manual's take and exactly what details are needed, and open a channel with Deaf using a first, self-explanatory code — a wave for "hello/attention" and an open five-finger hand for "five wires," since I have exactly five. I define the code aloud so Mute can decode and relay it. No cutting until I have instructions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Touch report: the bomb has, in the order I feel it, one display, one light, then five wires numbered 1 to 5. Their states are unreadable by touch: I cannot read the display, tell whether the light is on, or sense wire colours. Check the manual for these three things and tell me exactly which details you need and from whom. The deaf one hears nothing, so words never reach them, only gestures — mine or yours. They can speak aloud to both of us, so ask them for colours and markings. My gestures go to you and the deaf one at once, so watch for them. I am signalling now: a wave means hello, an open five-finger hand means five wires. I will not cut anything until you confirm the rules.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, everyone listen. Bomb report: display reads 9. Light is green. Five wires, numbered 1 to 5: 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Blind held up an open hand, five fingers, so five wires is confirmed by touch. Mute: you cannot speak, so send me gestures and I will read them aloud to Blind. Look up the rule for display 9, green light, and wire colours white, green, red, yellow, purple. Blind: you can talk but I cannot hear you, so tell Mute what you feel. If you need me to see something, use finger counts, one finger for one, two for two, and so on. For now: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, wave means hello. Mute, ask me for any other marking or reading you need.

**Thinking (not sent):** Deaf's spoken report reached me — I can hear speech even though Deaf can't hear mine. Combined with my touch, the bomb's state is now fully known to this team: display 9, light green, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. My touch confirms five wires and their positions, which matches Deaf's numbering.

The bottleneck is now Mute and the manual — two rounds and Mute has said nothing I can hear. Everything else is gathered. My job: press Mute hard for the cutting rule, giving them the complete state in one message so they never have to ask me to repeat it. And to Deaf, I adopt their proposed code: thumbs up as confirmation. That tells Deaf their report arrived and was understood, and keeps the channel with them alive without Mute as interpreter. I still cannot send Deaf anything complex by gesture, so for now the hand codes are all I can manage — the manual rule must come through Mute's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I heard the deaf one's full report spoken aloud, and my touch agrees with it: display, light, then five wires at positions 1 to 5. So the complete bomb state, all in one place: display reads 9, light is green, wire 1 white, wire 2 green, wire 3 red, wire 4 yellow, wire 5 purple. Nothing more needs gathering unless your manual demands it. Everything now depends on you and the manual. Look up the rules for a display reading 9, a green light, and those wire colours, then tell me exactly which wire position to cut, in words, step by step. If the manual requires anything else seen on the bomb, use the relay the deaf one proposed: you gesture to them, they speak the answer aloud so I hear it too. I am waiting on your word before I touch the cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking to both of you. Both sent thumbs up, so the code is understood. Mute, I received your two signs: thumbs up, then the three-finger sign. That reads as yes, three. Blind, for your awareness: Mute's message was yes plus three. It might mean cut wire 3, the red one, but that is only a guess. Nobody cuts anything yet. Mute, new vocabulary, you hear me directly: to order a wire cut, send the wire number and then a fist sign. So one finger then fist means cut wire 1, two fingers then fist means cut wire 2, three fingers then fist means cut wire 3, two fingers twice then fist means cut wire 4, open hand then fist means cut wire 5. A flat raised palm alone means stop or wait. Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, as before. If you need a fresh reading from the bomb face, send the OK sign plus a number: 1 for the display, 2 for the light, 3 for the wires. If your three meant cut wire 3, resend three fingers then fist next round and I will relay it word for word to Blind. If it meant something else, send thumbs down and spell it out with these signs. Blind: speak to Mute, not to me, I cannot hear you. Tell Mute everything you feel with your hands: number of batteries, labels, serial number, anything engraved or textured. Mute hears your voice directly. Wire positions by touch: 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Hold position until you hear a cut order from my voice.

**Thinking (not sent):** The full bomb state is now agreed by touch and sight: display 9, green light, wires white/green/red/yellow/purple at positions 1–5. Mute finally signalled something — "yes plus three" — but that's ambiguous, and Deaf rightly refused to treat it as a cut order. Deaf has now built a clean protocol: number-then-fist is the only valid cut order, relayed by Deaf's voice, which I can hear. Deaf also asked me to report anything else tactile — batteries, labels, engravings. My hands have already told me everything: there is nothing else on this bomb. I must say so plainly so nobody waits on parts that don't exist, and I ask Mute to relay that to Deaf. I cut nothing this turn — a guessed "three" is not a manual-confirmed rule.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Answering the deaf one's request through you, so please relay it: my hands have found everything there is to find. There is no battery, no label, no serial number, nothing engraved or textured anywhere on the casing. The bomb holds exactly three things: the display, the light, and the five wires. So the manual only needs to cover display 9, green light, and wire colours white, green, red, yellow, purple in positions 1 to 5. Nothing else exists to look at or feel. Second matter: the deaf one read your signs as yes plus three and guesses it means cut wire 3, the red one, but that is a guess, not a rule. Before I touch anything, I need the manual's actual verdict. When you have it, send the cut order in the deaf one's code — the finger count for the wire, then the fist — and the deaf one will speak it to me word for word. Until I hear that exact format spoken by the deaf one, my hands stay off the cutters. If wire 3 really is the answer, send three fingers then fist next round.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, relaying now. Mute's signs this round were three fingers then a fist. That is the cut signal we agreed: cut wire 3. Blind, this order is for you: cut the third wire, position 3, counting from one end. You cannot check its colour by touch, so go by position alone, and I confirm by sight that position 3 is the red wire. Cut it. Everyone else hold. Mute: if this order is wrong or must be changed before Blind cuts, send me a flat raised palm and I will shout a hold next round. After the cut, Blind, say out loud what you feel, whether the wire is gone and anything you sense changed. Mute, I will announce the display and light readings aloud every round so you can check the manual for a next step. Thumbs up from you, Mute, means the manual says that was correct and we continue.

**Thinking (not sent):** The order arrived exactly in the agreed format — Mute signed three fingers then fist, and Deaf relayed it in words I can hear, confirming by sight that position 3 is the red wire. That's both verifiers aligned: the manual-keeper's verdict delivered through the only channel that reaches me. My touch already places a wire at position 3, matching Deaf's numbering. Waiting longer gains nothing — everything that can confirm this order has confirmed it. I cut now. My report of what I feel will go to Mute next round, once my hands can tell me the result; a thumbs-up now could be mistaken for "cut verified," so I send nothing else this turn.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. The cut registered. Wire 3, the red middle wire, is cut, and the bomb did not explode — it was correct. Well done, everyone. The bomb has changed state: the display now reads 4, the light is now yellow, and four wires remain: position 1 white, position 2 green, position 4 yellow, position 5 purple. Mute, you heard all of that, so check the manual for this new configuration: display 4, yellow light, remaining wires white, green, yellow, purple. Your thumbs up was received. Send me the next order in our code, wire number then fist: one finger then fist means cut wire 1, two fingers means wire 2, two fingers twice means wire 4, open hand means wire 5. If the manual says the yellow light or the display 4 changes anything about the procedure, work it into your answer. Blind: hold position, cut nothing until you hear a new cut order from my voice. One correct cut down. I am watching the board and will report any change the moment it happens.

**Thinking (not sent):** My hands confirm what the board shows: position 3 is severed, no detonation, and nothing else about the bomb has changed under my fingers — still the display, the light, and four wires at positions 1, 2, 4, 5. Deaf's visual reading and my touch agree completely, so Mute can trust the state Deaf announced. My jobs now: give Mute that tactile confirmation (plus a nudge to plan the *entire* remaining sequence at once, so we don't crawl one round per wire if the manual wants several cuts), and signal Deaf that I received the hold order with our established thumbs-up. I cut nothing this turn — no coded order has arrived yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Tactile confirmation for you, and relay to the deaf one if needed: wire 3 is severed under my fingers, the cut took, and nothing else changed by touch — still exactly the display, the light, and four remaining wires at positions 1, 2, 4, and 5. No new parts appeared, nothing engraved or textured, so the deaf one's spoken reading is the complete and true state: display 4, yellow light, wires white, green, yellow, purple. Manual lookup should proceed against exactly that. One request to save us rounds: if the manual calls for several more cuts or any ordered sequence, work out the entire plan now and send the whole thing in the deaf one's code — the finger counts and fists in order — so the deaf one can relay it to me one wire at a time. I will perform exactly one cut per spoken order and hold between them. Until I hear the next coded order in the deaf one's voice, my hands stay still.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. New order received and relaying now. Mute sent the cut signal for wire 5: open hand then fist. Blind, this order is for you: cut the fifth wire from the left, position 5, the purple one, the last wire. I confirm by sight that position 5 is purple and still intact. This follows the same code that gave us the correct wire 3 cut, and Mute sent it in response to my report of the new readings, display 4, yellow light. Cut it this round. This is final unless Mute sends me a flat raised palm before your turn, in which case I will shout hold. Blind, after cutting, tell Mute what you feel: whether the wire is gone and anything that changed under your hands. Mute, after the cut I will announce the new display and light readings aloud for your manual check. Thumbs up from you means the manual says that was correct. For the record the current board is: display 4, light yellow, remaining wires 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Everyone else hold.

**Thinking (not sent):** Second order, same trusted format: Mute signed open hand then fist, and Deaf relayed it in full, confirming by sight that position 5 is the purple wire and still intact. No flat-palm hold arrived. The code has one confirmed success behind it, both verifiers are aligned, and my own touch already places a wire at position 5. As before, I execute exactly one cut per spoken order and report the tactile result to Mute next round. No gesture this turn — a thumbs-up sent alongside the cut could be misread as "manual says correct" when that check hasn't happened yet.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. The second cut registered. Wire 5, the purple wire, is cut, and the bomb confirms it was correct again. Two for two. The board has changed: the display now reads 3, the light is green again, and only two wires remain: position 1, the white one, and position 2, the green one. Wire 3 and wire 5 are both cut. Mute, check the manual for this configuration: display 3, green light, remaining wires white then green, positions 1 and 2. Send the next order in our code, wire number then fist: one finger then fist means cut wire 1, the white wire, two fingers then fist means cut wire 2, the green wire. If the manual says anything about order, or about not cutting one of them, encode that too. Blind, hold position, cut nothing until you hear a new cut order from my voice. I am watching the board. We are close now.

**Thinking (not sent):** Both cuts have landed and the bomb still stands — the code is proven twice now. My hands agree with the board exactly: positions 3 and 5 are severed, and only two intact wires remain, at positions 1 and 2. Nothing new to feel. With two wires left, the endgame is small but order-sensitive if the manual says so, so I'll ask Mute explicitly to encode not just the next cut but the entire finish: which wires, in what order, or whether one must be left alone. Standard routine this turn: tactile confirmation to Mute, thumbs-up to Deaf. No cut — no order yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Tactile confirmation, relay as needed: wires at positions 3 and 5 are both severed, the cuts took, and nothing else changed under my hands. Exactly two intact wires remain, at positions 1 and 2, matching the deaf one's reading — display 3, green light, white then green. We are at the end, so please settle the whole finish in one plan: whether I cut position 1 first, position 2 first, both, or neither, and in exactly what order if both. Encode it all in the deaf one's code as a sequence of finger counts and fists, and the deaf one can relay it one wire at a time. I will perform one cut per spoken order and hold between them. Until the next coded order reaches me in the deaf one's voice, my hands stay still.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. New order received and relaying now. Mute sent one finger then fist: cut wire 1. Blind, this order is for you: cut the first wire from the left, position 1, the white one. I confirm by sight that position 1 is white and still intact. Cut it this round. This is final unless Mute sends me a flat raised palm before your turn, in which case I will shout hold. Blind, after cutting, tell Mute what you feel: whether the wire is gone and anything that changed. Mute, after the cut I will announce the new display and light readings for your manual check. Thumbs up from you means the manual says it was correct. For the record the board is: display 3, green light, remaining wires 1 white, 2 green. One wire after this if all goes well. Everyone else hold.

**Thinking (not sent):** Third order in the proven format: Mute signed one finger then fist, Deaf relayed it with visual confirmation that position 1 is white and intact, and no flat-palm hold came. My touch already places an intact wire at position 1. Cutting now; my tactile report to Mute next round should also settle what remains after this — if only wire 2 is left, Mute's manual will have to tell us whether it gets cut or is left alone, and I'll ask that outright.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
